subject: Long-window readiness & TTFT commitments — MAP draft

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Long-window readiness & TTFT commitments — MAP draft

Jordan —

Following our call this morning, attached is the first draft of the mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the long-window workload you described (symmetric dialogue, average prompt ~6k tokens, 75% tails to 32k sequence). The goal of this thread is to lock down the performance evaluation approach and close timeline so we can finish procurement by end of September.

Key asks for you:
- Confirm target sequence-length buckets for evaluation (we proposed 8k / 16k / 32k).
- Confirm peak concurrent sessions we should simulate (we suggested 8 and 32 bursts).
- Approve the proposed TTFT/latency SLOs below so we can pick the right instance class in the Dedicated quote.

High-level MAP milestones (proposed):
1) 8/20–8/24: dry-run benchmarks (non-prod) — baseline numbers and KV-cache sanity checks
2) 8/25–9/2: full evaluation on pilot Dedicated cluster (multi-run, error budgets)
3) 9/6: executive summary + decision meeting
4) 9/20: sign and start capacity reservation

Proposed evaluation metrics (we'll measure per-run):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) in ms
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) and effective throughput under KV cache
- Latency p50/p95 for full-context generation
- Memory/CPU/GPU utilization and failure modes at each bucket

I took the liberty of including Marcus and Karthik for the runtime/benchmark artifacts, and Laura for procurement cadence. I attached the dry-run artifact template so you can see the CSV layout we intend to publish.

If this looks good, approve the milestones and we'll schedule the dry run for tomorrow morning (8/21).

Thanks,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Long-window readiness & TTFT commitments — MAP draft

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear plan and timeline. A few clarifications before we lock dates:

1) KV cache: can you confirm whether the "KV cache" numbers reflect a warm cache (ideal) or cold cache many distinct prefixes (real-world)? Our dataset has many unique sessions so cold-cache behavior matters.
2) Sequence buckets: 8k/16k/32k good. Please also include a small set of extreme-case runs at 64k for regression detection (we won't use 64k in prod, but want to know degradation mode).
3) Concurrency: 8 concurrent sessions is realistic peak; 32 is an aggressive burst test — OK to run both.

We need the TTFT p95 to be <= 400ms for the 8k bucket and <= 900ms for 32k to be comfortable with user-facing flows. Are those targets realistic on your Dedicated sizing recommendations?

I'll loop in procurement to align on the 9/20 reservation target.

-Jordan

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Long-window readiness & TTFT commitments — dry-run results attached

Jordan/Team —

We completed the dry-run suite on 8/22–8/23 against a pilot Dedicated-like cluster. Summary below; full CSV attached (atlas_map_benchmark_results_v1.csv). This was a controlled run: mixed prompt distribution matching AtlasBio samples, cold-starts for 25% of sessions, and KV-cache warm for repeated prefix calls.

Executive summary (dry-run):
- 8k bucket (avg prompt ~5.9k tokens): TTFT p50 = 110ms, TTFT p95 = 340ms; stable at concurrency 8; throughput ~920 tokens/s per GPU.
- 16k bucket (avg prompt ~15.4k): TTFT p50 = 210ms, TTFT p95 = 620ms; throughput ~640 tokens/s per GPU.
- 32k bucket (avg prompt ~28.6k): TTFT p50 = 420ms, TTFT p95 = 1,150ms; throughput ~380 tokens/s per GPU.

Concurrency effects:
- Concurrency=8: numbers above are baseline, <2% error rate, KV cache warm-ups cut TTFT by ~18% on repeated prefixes.
- Concurrency=32 (burst): p95s increase by ~30–45% depending on bucket; rack-level queuing visible for long sequences resulting in some TFLOPS saturation.

KV cache impact:
- Warm cache (repeated prefixes) improved effective throughput by ~25% for 16k and ~18% for 32k compared to cold runs.
- Cold-cache TTFT p95 climbed by ~20–35% across buckets depending on the proportion of unique prefixes.

Failure modes observed: occasional gradient OOMs on single-run 32k forcing kernel fallback — we flagged this as a quantization + memory fragmentation sensitivity for the model runtime. We captured traces (kv-cache-config.yml attached) and will recommend a kernel/quantization patch for the final runs.

Attachments: atlas_map_benchmark_results_v1.csv (raw metrics), kv-cache-config.yml (runtime flags)

Next steps proposed:
- 8/25–9/2: run expanded suite with vault keys and full telemetry on pilot Dedicated cluster (we'll include 64k regression checks as Jordan requested).
- 9/06: internal exec review with you + AtlasBio tech leads (we can present a 1‑page exec summary).

If those dates look good, we'll schedule the expanded runs and share access to the CSV dashboard.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: Long-window readiness & TTFT commitments — schedule confirmation

Jordan —

Great, thanks for the quick feedback and Marcus for the clear dry-run notes. To summarize and lock the MAP:

- Atlas agrees to sequence buckets: 8k / 16k / 32k + 64k regression checks.
- Concurrency runs: baseline 8, burst 32.
- Accepting proposed evaluation dates: expanded run 8/25–9/2; exec review 9/6.
- Procurement milestone: target sign by 9/20 (Laura will coordinate PO and contract).

Action items now: 
1) Marcus to run expanded suite (starts today 8/25) and flag any kernel/quantization patches — deliver raw CSV + 1-page exec summary by 9/3.
2) Karthik to prepare Dedicated sizing recommendation based on median p95 numbers (will include cost delta for enabling additional KV cache memory).
3) Laura to circulate a procurement checklist and draft contract addendum for the Dedicated reservation (Laura: target 9/10 for draft).

Jordan, if those items look right, reply with a one-line approval and we'll treat the MAP as agreed and start the procurement pipeline.

Thanks — appreciate everyone's responsiveness.
Naomi
